note: Grace Hill's six published partner programs, taken from gracehill.com/partnerships. The point of this file is that 'partner' is not one thing. A Training Partner means their content sits inside our LMS, which is a reason to buy us. An Integration Partner means data moves between the platforms. A Referral or Reseller Partner means revenue moves. Those three call for completely different behavior from a rep, and the old version of this file collapsed them into one warning.
rule: Partnership is context, not a gag order. A company can be a partner on one product and a competitor on another, and several of these are exactly that. Every partner record carries full compete information — the same verdict, gaps, questions and win themes as any other competitor. What the partnership changes is what you say about the RELATIONSHIP, not whether you compete on the PRODUCT.

programs.name: Training Partner Program
programs.official: brings together Grace Hill and industry partners to deliver high-quality training content for free to Grace Hill Training customers.
programs.whatItMeans: Their training content is delivered inside PerformanceHQ Training, free to our Training customers. If a property runs both companies' products, their people take that partner's training in the same place as everything else — one login, one transcript, one compliance report.
programs.repMove: Lead with the consolidation: the customer keeps the partner they like and stops managing a second system to get its training. If the deal ALSO has you competing with this company on a different product line, that is normal — compete there on the merits, and keep this line as the proof that we are not asking them to rip the partner out.
programs.watchFor: Do not present the partner's contributed content as proof of our own authoring depth. And do not assume the partnership covers their whole line — the overlap that matters is usually elsewhere in their catalog.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

programs.name: Integration Partnerships
programs.official: seamless access to partner solutions within our products or pushes customer data to the partner solutions they prefer.
programs.whatItMeans: The two platforms exchange data. Either their solution is reachable from inside ours, or we push customer data out to theirs. Several of these companies also sell products that compete with ours — that is normal and it is why the program exists.
programs.repMove: Compete on the specific module that overlaps, and only that module. If the prospect already runs the partner's platform, the integration is a buying reason: their data flows into ours on day one. Both things are true at once and a rep should say both.
programs.watchFor: Never characterize the parent company, its quality, or its roadmap. A Yardi or Entrata product competing with us does not make Yardi or Entrata a competitor — and the integration does not make their competing module off-limits.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

programs.name: Survey Partner Program
programs.official: connects survey clients with innovative solutions that directly address areas of improvement identified through resident and tenant feedback.
programs.whatItMeans: When a survey surfaces a problem, these are the partners we point customers at to fix it. They sit downstream of our data, on the action side of the loop rather than the measurement side.
programs.repMove: Use it as evidence the loop closes: the survey finds the issue and there is already a named route to fixing it. Where the same partner also sells measurement, compete there normally — separate the fix they provide from the measurement they sell before you say anything comparative.
programs.watchFor: Do not compete with a Survey Partner on the fix they provide; that is the part that makes us stronger. Do compete on measurement and benchmarking if they sell it — being downstream of us on one thing does not make them a partner on everything.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

programs.name: Referral and Reseller Partnerships
programs.official: partners receive qualified leads or Grace Hill receives referrals; select cases include reseller agreements for distributing partner content.
programs.whatItMeans: Revenue moves between us. We send them leads, they send us leads, and in some cases we resell their content. A person on their side may be compensated on a deal we source.
programs.repMove: Compete normally on any overlapping product — but keep every word strictly factual and sourced, and tell the partnership owner afterwards. Revenue moves between us and a person on their side may be compensated on a deal we sourced, so a loose comparative remark can land somewhere expensive.
programs.watchFor: The highest-sensitivity program in the list. Nothing unsourced, nothing about their company, nothing about the commercial terms. If a prospect asks directly whether we compete, the answer is yes on this product and we work together on that one — then bring in the partnership owner.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

programs.name: Thought Leadership and Marketing Partnerships
programs.official: co-branded education and industry insights, including webinars, content, sponsorships, and visibility.
programs.whatItMeans: Industry bodies and trade press we publish alongside. No product relationship. Often a route into a room rather than anything a rep sells against.
programs.repMove: Use the co-branded material as credibility and the relationship as an introduction path. If the body also runs a credential or a commercial training arm, that arm is a competitor and gets a normal competitive read — the association and its commercial arm are two different things.
programs.watchFor: Separate the association from its commercial arm before you say anything comparative. Never imply an industry body endorses us because we published alongside it.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

programs.name: Content Creation Partnerships
programs.official: partners develop high-quality training or thought leadership content for distribution on Grace Hill platforms.
programs.whatItMeans: They build course or thought-leadership content that ships on our platforms. Distinct from the Training Partner Program, where a partner contributes their existing content free — here they are building it for distribution with us.
programs.repMove: Part of the answer to "is your library deep enough?" — named specialist partners built parts of it. Say who, and what they specialize in. Where the same company sells a competing platform, compete on the platform and keep the content credit intact.
programs.watchFor: Do not imply we authored content a partner built, and do not present a partner's specialist library as proof of our own authoring capacity.
programs.competeRule: Full compete information applies. This program describes the relationship, not a restriction on competing.

elevate-mystery-shopping.title: Name collision — this is not our Elevate
elevate-mystery-shopping.line: This is a separate company at elevatemysteryshopping.com, unrelated to Grace Hill Elevate. Say the full company name out loud, and never let “Elevate” stand alone in a conversation where both could be meant.

The partnership sits elsewhere in the corporate family and is not a reason to soften this comparison, but it is a reason not to characterize CoStar as a company.

standingRules: Compete on the product in front of you. A partner's product competing with ours does not make the parent company a competitor, and a partnership on one line does not protect their product on another.
Name the partnership out loud when it comes up. A prospect who already runs the partner will hear about it eventually; hearing it from you first is worth more than the thirty seconds it costs.
Never disparage a partner, their product, or their company. Compete on what we do better, sourced, not on what they do badly.
Never state, imply, or speculate about the commercial terms of any partnership — revenue share, exclusivity, fees, or anything else.
Where the partnership is genuinely a reason to buy — their content already lives in our platform, their data already flows into ours — lead with that. It is a stronger position than competing.
Tell the partnership owner after a competitive deal against a partner. Not before, and not for permission — so the relationship side is never surprised by something they could have handled.

postureMeaning.reason-to-buy: The partnership is an asset in the deal. Lead with it — and still compete on any product that overlaps.
postureMeaning.compete-on-the-module: Compete on the overlapping product only. The parent company is not the competitor; their module is.
postureMeaning.downstream-of-us: They act on what our data finds. Compete only where they also measure, and use the rest as proof the loop closes.
postureMeaning.relationship-sensitive: Compete normally, but every word factual and sourced, and tell the partnership owner afterwards. Money or reputation moves between the companies.

retiredPosture: 'never-compete' was retired on 2026-08-23 by the VP of Product Marketing. It suppressed compete information on companies that genuinely compete with us on a product line, which left reps walking into those deals with nothing. Partnership type is now listed as context on every record and the compete information stays live.
